newsitem.title: JAPAN: Minor Metals--Japan Q2 chrome talks to start soon.
newsitem.headline: Minor Metals--Japan Q2 chrome talks to start soon.

text.p: Japanese negotiations with producers on charge chrome prices for the April-June period are set to start soon and local end-users are unlikely to accept prices above 45 cents a lb, local ferrochrome traders say.

Although prices in Europe were expected to rise to 47 cents a lb or higher, up five cents or more from the prior quarter, Japanese users are reluctant to accept higher prices due to sluggish demand here, they said.
"They'll probably get a better price in Europe," said one source from a leading Japanese trade house. Spot prices were said to be hovering around 47 to 48 cents a lb.
China's market for cobalt oxide remained flat, a trader in Hong Kong said, as buyers were waiting for the price, which fell 10 percent in the past month, to fall further.

A European trader in Hong Kong said Chinese importers were watching cobalt prices for further declines before placing orders. Prices of Russian material have fallen to about $17 a lb from $18.50/19.00 a lb two weeks ago.
Cobalt oxide, used in China in the manufacture of blue glass, now popular in the construction industry, and ceramics, was around $38 to $39 a kg, he said.

The bismuth market remained weak, traders said. One China trader said he was receiving offers for Russian material for the first time, possibly from Cold War-era stockpiles. This was keeping a lid on prices at $2.75 to $2.80 per lb, he said.
Conversion costs in China were cheaper than in most places in the world, he said, and the quality of the Chinese end product, ammonium para-tungsten, or APT, was good.
The number of Chinese factories was shrinking as the government sought to close big loss makers and transfer workers into other industries, sources said.

Chinese ferro-molybdenum prices were drifting, the European source said, with offers down from $11 a lb just weeks ago to $10.50 now. In London late last week, the metal was indicated at $11/$12 a kg ex-Europe.
"Oxide is falling, but it depends on demand. Demand is a little bit softer than people expected, especially in Europe. But it can pick up again," the trader said.

In the germanium market, a trader in southern China said that last week he sold 200 kg of 99.999 percent germanium oxide to Japanese users at $930 per kg. The trader said Chinese producers were now offering their material at $880 a kg.
In London late last week, the metal's price was indicated at $1,123/1,225 a kg.

Tokyo traders said they doubted that Albania's recent unrest would have much effect on its ferrochrome exports to Japan, adding that Japan imports only about 6,000 tonnes of ferrochrome a year from Albania, or a few percent of total imports.
